messages:
Leah (support): FYI customer ACME (acct acme-prod) opened a high-priority ticket — p99 latency jumped from ~900ms to 6-9s during last billing window. They're on a Dedicated pool. Ticket: INC-5421. Sample request IDs attached.

Leah (support): repro steps I used quickly: 
```
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\
  -H \"x-acme-req: a1b2c3\" \\
  -d '{"prompt":"short", "max_tokens":64}' \\
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Response times: 850ms -> 8.7s (p99). No 500s, just long attaches.

Ben (eng-oncall): Ack, looking. Can you paste one of the request IDs (x-acme-req) and the model+route? Also which Dedicated pool name?

Leah (support): Request IDs: a1b2c3, a1b2d4, a1b2e5. Pool: dedicated-eu-west-2-acme-1. Model: llama-2-13b-vf. Route: /v1/generate (default). Customer says it coincides with a billing-window burst ~T-15m.

Maya (sre): Checking pool metrics now — seeing attach queue spike and a bunch of cold GPU starts. Snapshot: queue-depth ~46, attach-latency p95=1.2s, p99=6.8s, GPU-warmups/sec low, pool utilization 92%. Looks like pool hit min_capacity then a surge caused concurrent attaches -> long handoff.

Maya (sre): Paste of quick grafana query (trimmed):
```
pool="dedicated-eu-west-2-acme-1" | attach_queue_depth: 46 | attach_latency_p99: 6800ms | cold_start_90pct: 750ms
```

Chris (eng-platform): This reads like Dedicated pool saturation + cold-gpu tail causing p99. Options: 1) temporary bump min_pool to 3 -> reduces cold starts, 2) prewarm a small set of GPUs before the billing window, 3) route that customer's priority traffic to a burst-capacity pool / hosted fallback. I can push a hotfix to scale config.

Maya (sre): Recommend immediate mitigation: increase min_pool from 1 -> 3 for that pool and enable prewarm=true for 15m during expected windows. That buys p99 reduction while we investigate autoscaler backoff. I can run the commands.

Maya (sre): Command I used to inspect and patch (kube-style):
```
# view pool
rctl get pool dedicated-eu-west-2-acme-1 --output=wide
# patch min size
rctl patch pool dedicated-eu-west-2-acme-1 --set 'spec.min_replicas=3'
```

deploy-bot: Started job deploy/patch-pool-1773012345 (user: Maya). Logs: applying patch -> success. New min_replicas=3. Warmup job queued.

Maya (sre): Warmup completed and we see attach-queue dropping to <5 within 90s. p99 dropped to ~1.1s on a quick sample. Will leave this config for 24h and monitor.

Ben (eng-oncall): Nice. Can platform follow up with a postmortem action: why didn't autoscaler scale earlier? Look at attach-threshold, randomized backoff, and image pull cold-starts. Also add a knob to prewarm by schedule for priority customers.

Chris (eng-platform): On it. Filing follow-up RFC and creating a short playbook: priority-customer-burst -> prewarm schedule + emergency min_pool patch. Linking doc: https://go.redwood/docs/ops/prewarm-playbook (internal).

Leah (support): I'll update ACME and their SREs with ETA and mitigation details. Thanks team — ticket INC-5421 now shows status: mitigated -> monitoring. :thumbsup:

Maya (sre): We'll keep an eye on p95/p99 over next 4 hours. If we see reformation of attach queue, we'll investigate image pull times and kernel hotplug stalls.

Ben (eng-oncall): Follow-ups:
- SRE to collect full flamegraph of attach path (Maya)
- Platform to review autoscaler thresholds + fairness (Chris)
- Support to coordinate SLA note with ACME (Leah)

Leah (support): Got it. I'll close loop with customer and escalate billing-window protections if needed.

Maya (sre): quick note — found two large containers resetting around T-10m causing concurrent image pulls. Opening infra issue INFRA-981 to track image-pull concurrency limits.

Chris (eng-platform): Adding temporary rate-limit to image pulls per node and a prefetch step for priority images. Will coordinate with infra team.

Leah (support): Closing comments to ACME sent. They'll watch and report regressions. Will reopen ticket if we see repeat p99.

Ben (eng-oncall): Thanks all. Leaving this thread open until 24h observation window passes.
